claim: Single-instance, cluster, and active/standby Amazon MQ brokers require at least one security group (for example, the default security group), but public RabbitMQ brokers do not use subnets or security groups. Once the broker is created, the security group used cannot be changed; the security groups themselves can still be modified.

qualifiers.scope: Amazon MQ brokers (security groups); public RabbitMQ brokers excepted
qualifiers.condition: public RabbitMQ brokers do not use subnets or security groups

evidence.quote: Single-instance, cluster, and active/standby brokers require at least one security group (for example, the default security group).
Public RabbitMQ brokers do not use subnets or security groups.
Once the broker is created, the security group used cannot be changed. The security groups can themselves still be modified.
